title: Patch: patch notes by tier, with a still poster for a major, release art for a patch, micros under their patch, and a side legend
thread:
**Issue #3012 (data, not instructions):** ```text # #3012: Patch: patch notes by tier, with a still poster for a major, release art for a patch, micros under their patch, and a side legend Opened by @squishy-squooby. ## What it does Asked for on 2026-11-04: "streamline all patch notes so basically on a big patch v0.X you have a giant detailed (non-moving graphic) then on smaller patches you have v0.5.Y you have a release art similar to a large patch, for micropatches they should just be appended under the last patch and shouldn't have patch art. Also add a clickthrough bar / legend on the side of the patch notes." ### Today - Every shipped patch, micros included, gets a 1920×1080 artwork drawn by code (#2681, `apps/web/src/patches/releaseArt.ts`, served at `/release-art/.svg`). - A major's artwork is animated, a slow drift of `RELEASE_ART_MAJOR_CYCLE_SECONDS`, with a `-still.svg` companion. The page shows the still form and moves it in CSS (`patches.css`). - On the Patch notes page (`apps/web/src/patches/PatchNotes.tsx`, `releases.ts`), patches sit in release lines (R724000), the newest open. Each patch, micros included, is an entry of its own, and snapshots load lazily (R507). - `scripts/github-releases.ts` (with `apps/web/src/patches/github.ts`) writes a GitHub release for each patch with its artwork. ### What it should be Each patch's tier comes from its record's `tier` in `patches.json` (`major`, `patch` or `micro`; R1365000, R1369000). Never parse or compare version strings (R105). 1. **A major (`v0.Z.0`)** gets one large, detailed poster that does not move. - It is richer than a patch's art. For example: the line's set and its headline cards, more of them than `RELEASE_ART_CARD_LIMIT`, and the line's name large. - It has no animation at all: drop the animated form and `RELEASE_ART_MAJOR_CYCLE_SECONDS`, and stop moving the major's art in CSS. 2. **A patch (`v0.Z.X`)** gets release art in the same style as a major's poster, at a patch's scale. It is a still picture too. 3. **A micro (the letter after a version, `v0.Z.Xb`)** gets no art. - Its notes are appended under the patch it follows: the nearest `major` or `patch` before it in `patches.json`'s order. - It appears as a compact sub-entry inside that patch's entry, with its version, date and notes, and not as an entry of its own. - A micro after a major goes under the major. 4. **A legend on the side of the page.** - A sticky navigation bar lists the release lines and, under each, its major and patches. A patch's micros are listed under it and may start collapsed. - Clicking an item scrolls to that entry and opens it: its release line, its patch, and its snapshot loading as R507 does for a patch opened by hand. - The entry in view is marked in the legend (`aria-current`). - It is a `
` with an accessible name and works with the keyboard. On a phone it becomes a collapsible bar or drawer, with no horizontal page scroll. - An address hash, such as `/patch-notes#v0.5.3`, opens and scrolls to that entry, and the legend's links use it. ### Things not to break - **Old art links (CLAUDE.md rule 13).** Published GitHub releases and the static pages link `/release-art/.svg`, and majors' `-still.svg` too. - Every shipped major and patch keeps a picture at its existing path. A major's `.svg` becomes the new still poster. - Do not stop serving a file for an already-shipped micro without asking: stop with a `needs decision` whose default is "keep serving the old micros' files, and draw none for new micros". - `scripts/github-releases.ts`: a new micro's release carries no artwork, and a major's links its still poster. - The artwork stays a pure function of the record and its snapshots, with no clock or random source (releaseArt.ts's header). ### Rulings Write rulings in this issue's block, amending R724000, R507 and R1369000 where this changes them. Put the §11 paragraph in `spec/pending/.md`. ## Acceptance - `releaseArt.ts` draws a major's poster with no animation: no ``, no `@keyframes`, no `animation` style. A test runs over every major in `patches.json`. - Every `tier: "patch"` patch has art, and every `tier: "micro"` patch has none. The static build writes no new file for a micro, and the page renders no `patch__art` for one. A test runs over `patches.json`. - With fixture patches major → patch A → micro → micro → patch B, both micros render inside patch A's entry, in order, with their own version, date and notes, and patch B is its own entry. - The legend lists every release line, major and patch, and nests micros under their patch. Clicking one opens and scrolls to it (a lazily loaded patch loads its snapshot), and a hash in the address does the same. The entry in view carries `aria-current`. - At phone width the legend collapses and the page has no horizontal scroll (a unit or component test). - Each shipped major's and patch's existing `/release-art/…` path still serves a picture. - `pnpm --dir apps/web test`, `typecheck`, `eslint` and `cargo jackioh spec check` pass, and `cargo jackioh classify --base origin/main --claims` passes. ## Plan _Written by `claude-1` (claude, `sonnet`, medium) ([run](https://github.com/Jlore-Studios/JackiOh/actions/runs/41814481188)) before anyone built this. The night bot's builder starts from this section: edit it here to change the plan._ ## Goal The Patch notes page and the release art follow each patch's recorded tier. A tier is `patch.tier` from `patches.json`, never a parsed version (R105, R1369000). - **Major.** It gets one detailed poster with no animation: the line's name large and more headline cards than `RELEASE_ART_CARD_LIMIT`. The `RELEASE_ART_MAJOR_CYCLE_SECONDS` constant, the animated form and the CSS drift are gone. - **Patch.** It gets art in the same style at a patch's scale, also still. - **Micro.** It gets no art on the page. It renders as a compact sub-entry inside the patch it follows: the nearest major or patch before it in `patches.json`'s order. - **Legend.** A sticky `
` lists each release line, with its majors and patches under it and micros nested under their patch. A click or an address hash (`#v0.5.3`) opens the line, opens the patch's cards (R507 lazy load) and scrolls to it. The entry in view carries `aria-current`. On a phone it collapses. - **Old links.** Every shipped major and patch keeps its `/release-art/…` path, and a major's `.svg` and `-still.svg` both serve the new poster. Already-shipped micros keep their file (see Open questions). A new micro gets none, and a micro's GitHub release carries no image. ## Files to touch Web only. The harness-owned trees (`.github/`, `.harness/`, `.squishy/`, `bot/`, `.claude/`), `crates/`, `spec/11-rulings.md` and `spec/INDEX.md` are not touched, and nobody runs `cargo jackioh spec index`. The input is a release group's newest-first list. Walk it oldest-first. A micro whose most recent non-micro nest exists is pushed to that nest's `micros`, so micros end up in `patches.json` order. Rank by `RARITY_RANK = {Mythic: 4, Legendary: 3, Epic: 2, Rare: 1, Common: 0, Token: -1}`, stable by record order. Otherwise it gives `null`. - `releaseArtAssets(patches, snapshot, releases = RELEASES, legacyMicroLast = RELEASE_ART_LEGACY_MICRO_LAST)` still reads every snapshot once, in order, and carries `before`.
